title: Visa layoffs: Thousands of jobs slashed at the payments giant as CEO memo points toward AI acceleration
excerpt: The cuts come as the company faces an ever-changing payments landscape, increasingly disrupted by smaller, nimbler fintech startups.
content_html:
Visa Inc. is preparing to lay off about 2,600 workers, or about 7% of its workforce, the payments processing giant confirmed with Fast Company.

Most Read from Fast Company

  • Internet-famous bald eagle Jackie is fighting for her life as donations pour in to save Big Bear habitat

  • Warren Buffett is often asked what the ideal workplace is. His answer is the best career tip you'll hear today

  • How 'wildflowering' at work could lead to promotions

The cuts come as the company faces an ever-changing payments landscape, increasingly disrupted by smaller, nimbler fintech startups, and as it focuses more on AI-driven efficiency gains. Here's what you need to know.

What's happened?

On Tuesday, media outlets including Bloomberg reported that Visa is getting ready to lay off about 2,600 workers. That represents about 7% of the company's roughly 34,000-strong workforce.

The cuts were first disclosed to Visa's employees via a memo from CEO Ryan McInerney. Visa confirmed the layoffs and the accuracy of the memo's excerpts to Fast Company.

In the memo, McInerney said the layoffs would primarily affect the company's product and technology teams, stating he has a "deep conviction that we are doing what is right for Visa, our clients and our partners as we continue to focus on driving efficiency across the company in order to reinvest in our highest potential opportunities."

Visa will use some of the savings from its layoffs to reinvest in commercial and money-movement solutions, consumer payments, and value-added services, including stablecoins, Bloomberg reported.

In other words, the job cuts aren't so much about cost-cutting as they are about freeing up capital to invest in other areas.

AI was also a factor in the job reductions, McInerney confirmed in the memo.

"To capture the opportunities ahead and best position Visa to lead this transformation, we must continue evolving how we work," the CEO wrote. "AI is also helping to accelerate this evolution and shape the way work gets done at Visa."

Visa isn't alone in cutting fintech jobs

When it comes to the payments and larger fintech industry, Visa is hardly alone in its workforce reductions.

Back in January, Mastercard announced roughly 1,500 job cuts (or about 4% of its workforce). Like Visa, Mastercard at the time cited the desire to free up its capital to reinvest in other, more strategic areas.

In February, fintech startup Block announced 4,000 job cuts amidst an AI push, and in May PayPal laid off around 4,700 employees.

Visa reports Q3 2026 results today

  • 沃伦·巴菲特经常被问到理想的工作场所是什么。 他的回答是你今天听到的最好的职业建议

此次裁员之际，该公司面临着不断变化的支付格局，越来越多地受到规模较小、更灵活的金融科技初创公司的干扰，并且该公司更加关注人工智能驱动的效率提升。 这是您需要了解的内容。

发生了什么事？

周二，彭博社等媒体报道称，Visa 正准备裁员约 2,600 名员工。 这占该公司约 34,000 名员工的约 7%。

Visa 首席执行官瑞安·麦金纳尼 (Ryan McInerney) 在一份备忘录中首次向 Visa 员工披露了此次裁员计划。 Visa 向《Fast Company》证实了此次裁员以及备忘录摘录的准确性。

麦金纳尼在备忘录中表示，裁员将主要影响公司的产品和技术团队，并表示他“坚信我们正在做对 Visa、我们的客户和我们的合作伙伴有利的事情，同时我们将继续专注于提高整个公司的效率，以便对我们最具潜力的机会进行再投资。”

据彭博社报道，Visa 将利用裁员节省的部分资金再投资于商业和货币流动解决方案、消费者支付以及包括稳定币在内的增值服务。

换句话说，裁员与其说是为了削减成本，不如说是为了释放资金投资其他领域。

麦金纳尼在备忘录中证实，人工智能也是裁员的一个因素。

这位首席执行官写道：“为了抓住未来的机遇并让 Visa 处于领先地位以引领这一转型，我们必须继续改进我们的工作方式。” “人工智能还有助于加速这一演变，并塑造 Visa 的工作方式。”

Visa并不是唯一一家削减金融科技岗位的公司

在支付和更大的金融科技行业方面，Visa并不是唯一一家裁员的公司。

早在一月份，万事达卡就宣布裁员约 1,500 人（约占员工总数的 4%）。 与 Visa 一样，万事达卡当时也表示希望释放资金，以重新投资于其他更具战略意义的领域。

2 月份，金融科技初创公司 Block 宣布在人工智能推动下裁员 4,000 人，5 月份 PayPal 解雇了约 4,700 名员工。

Visa 今天公布 2026 年第三季度业绩
